memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"Then the LORD said to Moses, 'I will rain down bread from heaven for you. The
people are to go out each day and gather enough for that day. In this way I will
test them and see whether they will follow my instructions.'" - Ex 16:4 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God's response to their accusation is astonishing. They have just said He
brought them out to kill them. He answers by feeding them.

That is grace. Not a rebuke, not a lecture, but bread. Paul writes that "God
demonstrates his own love for us in this: While we were still sinners, Christ
died for us" (Rom 5:8). God's kindness does not wait for us to deserve it.

Now notice the arrangement: enough for that day, gathered daily. God could have
sent a month's supply at once. He deliberately did not.

And He says why: "In this way I will test them." The test was not whether they
could survive on little. It was whether they would trust Him tomorrow. A
storehouse would have made faith unnecessary. Daily bread kept them looking up
every morning.

Jesus taught us to pray in exactly this shape: "Give us today our daily bread"
(Matt 6:11). Not this year's supply. Today's.

Most of us would prefer the storehouse. We want provision secured far enough
ahead that we need not depend on anyone. God's way is often to give enough,
today, and to invite us back tomorrow.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Would you rather have God's daily provision or a year's security?
2. What has God given you today that is genuinely enough?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, thank You for feeding me even when I have complained. Teach me to trust
You for today and to come back to You tomorrow. Amen.
